subject: Next steps: procurement readiness & signatory lanes for Redwood pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbuslogistics.com>, Rajesh Malhotra <rajesh.malhotra@nimbuslogistics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood pilot discovery - procurement & approvals

Hi Samantha / Rajesh — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we all have the same view.

Call highlights
- Primary use case: generative document summarization for inbound freight exceptions (low latency, high throughput).
- Pilot scope: 3 warehouses, 2 weeks of live traffic ingestion, SLOs: 95th percentile < 350ms.
- Data classification: PII present in manifests; customer requires audit logs and optional tokenization.

Procurement & commercial questions we flagged
- Budget owner (finance signatory) and who approves PO vs card.
- Preferred purchase flow (PO system / marketplace / card).
- Contract cadence: SOW + PoC addendum, MSA and PO signoff timeline.
- Any required security questionnaires (SOC2 / penetration test evidence).

Ask from your side
1) Please confirm the budget owner / economic buyer and the signatory path for a $50k pilot.
2) Confirm whether Nimbus will use PO (Coupa/ServiceNow) or a credit card for initial payment, and any internal procurement ticketing process.
3) Share contact for procurement (ticket queue or person) and an approximate procurement lead time.

We have attached a short one-pager on PO vs card flows and a draft SOW template to speed approvals. If it helps, we can present the commercial path to procurement in their ticket system.

Proposed next step: 30-minute handoff with your finance/procurement lead + our commercial/ops team — suggested window: Monday 4/26, 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks — I will pull in pricing and an SOW draft once you confirm payment method.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_PO-vs-Card-OnePager.pdf, Redwood_SOW_template.pdf
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@nimbuslogistics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajesh Malhotra <rajesh.malhotra@nimbuslogistics.com>, procurement@nimbuslogistics.com
Date: 2027-04-24T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood pilot discovery - procurement & approvals

Camila — thanks for the summary and for the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget owner / signatory: Rajesh Malhotra (Finance Director) will own the budget for this pilot. For any spend > $10k the signatory is our VP of Finance, but Rajesh can approve the pilot and route a PO.
- Payment method: Nimbus prefers PO via ServiceNow for anything over $5k. Cards are used only for ad-hoc small purchases (< $5k).
- Procurement contact: procurement@nimbuslogistics.com (our intake queue). Typical turnaround for a standard PO is 7–10 business days once the SOW + pricing are submitted.
- Marketplace: we currently do not buy through marketplaces for infra/software (evaluating marketplace pilots later this year).
- Security: procurement will ask for SOC2 Type II and a basic data flow diagram; any pen-test summary is helpful but not required for a pilot.

I uploaded our completed RFI responses (attached) — the intake team prefers a single SOW + pricing doc to start the PO flow.

Happy to do the handoff on Monday 4/26; Rajesh is available 10:00–10:30 PT.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Product Operations
Nimbus Logistics
samantha.ortiz@nimbuslogistics.com

2) I'll prepare the commercial packet (SOW with line-item pricing, pilot acceptance criteria, invoice instructions for PO) and upload to HubSpot by EOD 4/25. Link to doc will be in the calendar invite.
3) Monica — can you put together a 1-page technical appendix highlighting data handling, tokenization options, and audit log capabilities (we should call out SOC2 controls and retention windows)? Aim to have that uploaded before the meeting.
4) Marissa — can you review any standard redlines we should accept for a pilot (term, liability cap) so Ben's packet is procurement-friendly?

If procurement turnaround is ~7–10 business days after SOW submission, we should be in a position for an early-May start if approvals flow.
